title: Declarative tool and agent definition
subtitle: In my agent runtime a tool is a YAML declaration and an agent class is a composition.

stats.label: declarative tools in the catalog, beside about twenty Rust built-ins
golden fixtures run through the runtime's own pipeline

lede: Every new agent tends to arrive with its own tooling and permissions, and every one of those is a new place for something to go wrong, so in Agent Swarm I decided tools and agent roles would be data. Tools are declared in YAML in four kinds. Composed tools template from inputs and earlier results, with recursion detection and depth caps; HTTP templates use RFC 3986 encoding; and a peer service turns any agent into a tool provider. A WebAssembly tool kind is declared and the harness rejects it, because a half-finished kind would have meant a partial bypass of the pipeline.
quote: Exceptions are where the holes are.
evidence: Agent tool design: 40 declarative tools in YAML across four kinds, validated in strict mode and pushed through 50 golden fixtures.
Agent orchestration: 29 personas declared, not coded, with model, provider and container kept in separate execution profiles.
Security testing for agent tools: injection fixtures that attack every shell template, and a tool without tests fails the build.
author: Corey James
